paper-tale-two-methods-unveiling-2024.summary: This paper proposes a comprehensive set of quality metrics (covering realism, diversity, novelty, and protocol compliance) for evaluating synthetic legitimate network traffic, and uses them to empirically compare several network-flow generation methods including GAN-based approaches and Bayesian Networks. Across two feature sets and a third dataset, the authors find that Bayesian Networks generally outperform GAN-based generators on their proposed metrics while being far cheaper computationally. CTGAN is run as one of seven benchmarked traffic generators, its training time, correlation-capture, and mode-invention behavior analyzed in detail alongside E-WGAN-GP and NetShare.

paper-general-image-classification-model.summary: This paper presents a general image-classification model for recognizing the operating modes of agricultural machinery from trajectory data, aiming to support precision-agriculture applications such as monitoring field operations. CTGAN is cited in the reference list, but with no visible citing sentence or abstract the manner of use cannot be established.

paper-interpretable-framework-identify-r.summary: The paper proposes an interpretable framework for identifying treatment-responsive subgroups in randomized clinical trials, combining an ensemble uplift-tree method with a sparse linear ranking model, and applies it to a failed intracerebral hemorrhage trial (ATACH2) augmented with historical controls. To address the trial's small sample size, the authors generate synthetic patient data and compare augmentation strategies using Qini-coefficient evaluation. CTGAN (and the bundled TVAE model) is trained with default parameters to produce synthetic treatment and control patients, and the CTGAN-augmented cohort yields the best downstream HTE estimation performance, making CTGAN's tabular GAN a load-bearing component of the empirical pipeline.

paper-drgat-predicting-drug-responses-20.summary: This paper introduces DRGAT, a drug-response prediction method that combines a denoising diffusion implicit model for data augmentation with a graph attention network exploiting high-order neighbor propagation over gene-expression data, reporting improved AUROC over state-of-the-art baselines. In its related-work discussion of prior data-augmentation approaches for gene-expression datasets, it briefly cites GAN-based tabular generative models (Xu et al., 2019) as having proposed universal tabular generative models applicable to GE data. CTGAN is mentioned only as prior art in this discussion, not run or benchmarked in the study.

paper-differentially-private-generation-.summary: This paper formalizes the problem of generating differentially private synthetic data when the input contains missing values, proposing three adaptive strategies that improve utility across four real-world datasets under varying missingness patterns and privacy budgets. It also derives tighter privacy bounds for incomplete data by modeling the missing mechanism as a sampling process. The SDV framework is cited as prior work on synthetic data generation, with no indication in the available evidence that its code was run.

paper-front-running-attack-detection-202.summary: This conference paper proposes cPacGAN, a method combining the conditional tabular GAN design with PacGAN's packed-sample discriminator to generate synthetic Ethereum transaction data for improving front-running attack detection with classifiers such as TabNet. The authors describe their approach as leveraging "Conditional Tabular GAN" to address class imbalance and mode collapse in tabular blockchain data, but the full text shows no library import, package name, or implementation detail beyond this prose description and the reference-list citation. CTGAN's conditional design is cited as the conceptual basis for the proposed generator, not run via the sdv-dev package.

paper-generative-model-decision-trees-20.summary: This AAAI-24 paper proposes GENTREE, a generative model for decision trees that learns a latent 'Tree-VAE' representation of pre-trained decision trees and uses a genetic algorithm to search that latent space for compact, accurate trees, comparing against classical, optimal, and ensemble tree induction methods. The single reference to the SDV family is a passing citation of the CTGAN paper (Xu et al. 2019) as the source of a generic 'VAE architecture,' unrelated to running or adapting any SDV code; the paper's own 'TVAE' denotes 'Tree-VAE,' not SDV's tabular VAE synthesizer.

paper-identification-synthetic-source-po.summary: This conference paper investigates whether the original data points used to create a synthetic dataset can be re-identified from the synthetic output, using Euclidean, Manhattan, Jaccard and Cosine distance measures fed into an MLP classifier, achieving about 90% accuracy in distinguishing source from non-source points. The synthetic dataset is generated by fitting a TVAE model, described by the authors as implemented in the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) library, with the number of training epochs tuned using SDV's overall quality score, column shape and column pair trend metrics. SDV's TVAE synthesizer and its quality-report metrics are run directly to produce and evaluate the synthetic data that the entire re-identification experiment is built on.

paper-ability-developers-training-preser.summary: This paper investigates whether learnware components can preserve or leak the training data of their developers, situating the discussion within work on privacy-preserving data release and synthetic data. CTGAN is mentioned only as one of several prior works on synthetic data generation and privacy protection, listed alongside differential-privacy and disclosure-risk papers, with no experiment run using it.

paper-private-synthetic-generation-mixed.summary: This paper proposes a hybrid private synthetic data generation pipeline for mixed-type datasets that combine structured and unstructured (text) columns, evaluated on Yelp reviews and drug side-effects data using a context-aware exposure metric alongside quality and privacy measures. In describing the structured-data component of their pipeline, the authors note that any GAN-based tabular synthesizer could be plugged in, citing CTGAN as one such option alongside TableGAN and UniformGAN. CTGAN is discussed as a candidate module for the structured-data stage rather than confirmed as the model actually run in their reported experiments.

paper-synthesis-hybrid-consisting-chest-.summary: This paper proposes a method to generate synthetic hybrid medical data combining chest X-ray images and tabular clinical records for COVID-19 patients, by encoding CXRs with a pretrained auto-encoding GAN (αGAN), merging the encoded features with tabular clinical variables, and training a tabular generative model on the combined representation before decoding synthetic images back out. The resulting synthetic dataset was evaluated by comparing patient-outcome prediction performance when trained on real, synthetic, or combined data. CTGAN, obtained as the stand-alone sdv-dev/CTGAN library, is run directly as the generative network for the merged tabular-plus-encoded-image records, making it the core engine of the paper's synthesis pipeline.

paper-synthetic-generate-avatar-demand-2.summary: This paper presents an extensive utility and privacy assessment of avatar-based synthetic data generation for healthcare-style tabular data, comparing it against several other synthesis methods (CT-GAN, SynthPop, MST, K-anonymity, SAIPH) using GDPR-inspired privacy criteria and utility metrics, and proposes an improvement based on conditional sampling in the latent space to allow on-demand synthetic data generation. The SDV quality score is used throughout as the main utility metric across all compared baselines, and CT-GAN is run as one of the comparative data-synthesis baselines.

paper-comparison-synthetic-approaches-ut.summary: This paper reviews and empirically compares three families of synthetic (reproduced) data generation methods -- sequential regression, nonparametric Bayesian multiple imputation, and deep generative models -- using a Korean national business survey dataset, evaluating them with utility metrics (pMSE, KL divergence, Wasserstein distance, CI overlap) and disclosure-risk metrics (identity/attribute disclosure risk, CAP). It finds CTGAN and TVAE achieve the lowest disclosure risk but the poorest utility among the compared methods. CTGAN and TVAE are described as easily usable through the Python library SDV and are run as the deep generative model baselines whose synthetic output is evaluated alongside sequential regression and Bayesian approaches.

paper-addressing-class-imbalance-tabular.summary: This paper tackles class imbalance in a simulated cancer intracellular-signaling dataset by using a generative-adversarial approach to oversample the minority class before applying supervised classifiers such as K-NN, reporting improved minority-class accuracy over the unbalanced baseline. The paper defines CTGAN as a conditional GAN variant purpose-built for tabular data in its background discussion, framing the type of model the authors' oversampling approach draws on. CTGAN is cited as the conceptual basis for the tabular GAN oversampling technique used, though the text available does not confirm whether SDV's own implementation was run.

paper-analyzing-proficiency-patterns-tes.summary: This conference paper applies clustering algorithms to student machine-learning test-result data to identify proficiency patterns useful for personalized learning and test design. The title's reference to 'augmentation algorithms' and the citation of the CTGAN paper suggest synthetic data augmentation was used to expand the student dataset, but the abstract itself does not describe this in detail. CTGAN is cited in connection with the augmentation step, but the exact usage cannot be confirmed from the available evidence.

paper-deep-learning-driven-techniques-20.summary: This paper introduces two generative techniques for synthesising irregular, multimodal real-time health and physical records -- the Temporally Correlated Multimodal GAN (TC-MultiGAN) and a Document Sequence Generator -- and evaluates them on a real-world use case from the H2020 GATEKEEPER healthcare AI project. TC-MultiGAN's quality is benchmarked in a results table against several prior GAN approaches (labelled CGAN, Gaussian Copula, Dragan GAN, Cramer GAN) using Wasserstein distance, KS test and correlation metrics. The 'CGAN' baseline row is cited to the CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019) paper, and a separate mention credits 'TGAN' with preserving inter-column mutual information, also citing the CTGAN paper -- so CTGAN is run (or reimplemented under a different name) as one of several numeric comparison baselines against the authors' own model.

paper-origami-energy-2023.summary: Builds a data-driven framework for predicting energy absorption in origami-inspired metamaterials, where each training sample requires an expensive folding simulation and datasets are therefore tiny. CTGAN's conditional generation supplies the additional samples the surrogate model needs, an application of SDV in mechanical metamaterial design rather than record synthesis.

paper-intrusion-detection-without-attack.summary: This conference paper surveys and experimentally tests strategies for training anomaly-based intrusion detectors without prior knowledge of attacks, ranging from shallow machine learning to deep learning and computer-vision-inspired out-of-distribution methods. The authors show that such detectors work well when normal and anomalous data distributions are clearly separable but degrade sharply on more realistic, complex datasets. The work cites the SDV (2016) and TGAN (2018) papers, likely in connection with synthetic/out-of-distribution tabular data generation, though no passage confirms these tools were actually run.

paper-learning-class-imbalanced-misclass.summary: This paper proposes a generative adversarial network approach that focuses on misclassified samples to address class-imbalanced learning problems, aiming to improve minority-class classification performance. The evidence available is limited to metadata showing a citation to the 2018 TGAN paper, with no citing sentence or abstract text obtained. TGAN is cited, but there is no indication it was run or compared against in the empirical work.

paper-non-imaging-medical-synthesis-2023.summary: A tutorial-style survey covering algorithms, evaluation methods, and limitations for synthesizing non-imaging medical data (clinical measurements, signals, EHRs) to support trustworthy AI in healthcare. The paper reviews deep generative approaches including autoencoders, GANs, and statistical methods, situating tabular synthesis GANs as prior art. CTGAN and its predecessor TGAN are described in detail as representative tabular data synthesis methods -- including TGAN's mode-specific normalization and CTGAN's conditional synthesis strategy for categorical features -- and the original Synthetic Data Vault paper is cited, but none of these are run by the authors.

paper-prediction-maximum-temperature-ris.summary: This conference paper addresses the scarcity of standardized datasets for computational dosimetry research by statistically modeling limited real data on incident power density and resultant skin temperature rise for RF exposure at 10-90 GHz, then sampling a synthetic dataset from the fitted model. Surrogate models trained on this synthetic data are shown to predict maximum temperature rise with low error on real held-out data, reducing reliance on costly electromagnetic simulations. The synthetic training data is manufactured using the Gaussian copula implementation cited to the SDV paper, making it the generator underlying the paper's entire empirical demonstration.

paper-importance-capturing-power-system-.summary: This paper develops a probabilistic resource adequacy (RA) assessment framework by adapting a production cost model and applies it to an IEEE Reliability Test System case study, examining which operational details -- multi-year data, storage dispatch, transmission limits -- matter for accurate RA evaluation. The paper cites the original Synthetic Data Vault paper, likely in relation to the data enhancement component, but no full text was available to confirm how or whether SDV software was actually run.

paper-generative-adversarial-networks-im.summary: A systematic review surveying GAN architectures and their applications across agricultural computer-vision tasks (plant health, weeds, fruits, aquaculture, animal farming, phenotyping, postharvest inspection). Among the many surveyed studies, the review describes a cited work (Ahmed et al., 2021) that used conditional tabular GAN to expand sensor data for a poultry/animal-farming classification task, reporting 97% accuracy with TabNet. CTGAN appears only as a described method within a third-party study cited in the review's survey table, not as something the review authors themselves run.

paper-energy-consumption-tgan-skip-2021.summary: Targets the forecasting errors that cause energy suppliers to over- or under-contract capacity, arguing that the training data available is too sparse for reliable prediction. The contribution is architectural rather than applied: TGAN-skip-Improved-WGAN-GP extends TGAN with skip connections and a modified objective, making this a named descendant of the first-party tabular GAN.

paper-population-synthesis-urban-residen.summary: This paper presents a machine learning approach to synthesize populations of residents for upcoming real estate developments, using a real dataset from Ecopark Township in Hanoi, Vietnam. It compares a Conditional Variational Auto-Encoder and a Conditional GAN, finding the CVAE outperforms both an empirical baseline and the CGAN for estimating population distributions. CTGAN is cited in the literature review as prior work on GAN-based tabular data generation but is not run in the experiments.

paper-synthetic-use-exploring-use-2021.summary: A review article exploring seven use cases for synthetic data within the pharmaceutical industry, covering data sharing, privacy protection, software testing, training, and other applications, and discussing generation methods and quality metrics with input from industry viewpoints. The SDV project website is cited only in passing, as one of two references supporting a claim that the pharmaceutical industry has matured its data-sharing systems and processes.

paper-model-generate-dynamic-synthetic-2.summary: This paper presents a PhD-project conceptual model and algorithms for generating dynamic, statistically representative synthetic test data for cross-organizational integration testing of the Norwegian National Registry modernization project. It surveys related synthetic data generation approaches and argues that existing methods, including relational database synthesis and probabilistic domain-model simulation, cannot address the need for dynamic, event-driven test data. The paper cites Patki et al.'s Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) as prior work that builds a statistical model of a relational database and samples from it, but critiques it as limited to stand-alone relational databases with no mechanism for updating generated data, and does not run or extend SDV.

paper-application-research-improved-yolo.summary: This paper proposes an improved YOLO V3 object detection algorithm for identifying electronic components on printed circuit boards, combining real PCB photos with virtual PCB images to form a joint training dataset, and adjusts the network's output layers and anchor boxes to boost detection accuracy to 93.07% mAP. In its introduction, the authors cite the Synthetic Data Vault paper only as prior evidence that general-purpose synthetic data generators have been built to enable data science, without using SDV software or methods in their pipeline.

paper-retabsyn-rl-2026.summary: Fine-tunes a language-model tabular generator with reinforcement learning against a reward built from feature-target correlation preservation, on the argument that matching the full joint distribution is unnecessary and data-hungry when downstream utility is bounded by feature mismatch and conditional-distribution mismatch alone, and reports gains over interpolation, diffusion, autoregressive and other RL-guided generators in low-sample, class-imbalanced and distribution-shifted regimes. SDV appears on both sides of the evaluation: TVAE is run from the official SDV library implementation at its default settings as one of six baselines, and the Shape and Corr. columns of the fidelity table are SDMetrics measures, with marginal similarity aggregated from Kolmogorov-Smirnov and total-variation scores and pairwise correlation similarity computed with contingency similarity for categorical pairs and a mixed-type method, cited to DataCebo's Synthetic Data Metrics.

preprint-causaldifftab-mixed-type-causal.summary: This preprint introduces CausalDiffTab, a diffusion-model-based generator for mixed-type tabular data (numerical and categorical) that adds a hybrid adaptive causal regularization method to improve fidelity without sacrificing generative quality, evaluated across seven benchmark datasets against nine baseline synthesizers. CTGAN and TVAE, both from the SDV-family CTGAN paper, are run as two of the nine baseline methods for comparison on shape/trend fidelity, privacy (DCR), and downstream ML utility metrics. SDV's CTGAN (mode-specific normalization) and TVAE are benchmarked against, not extended, in this evaluation.
preprint-causaldifftab-mixed-type-causal.needs: Not verified whether CTGAN/TVAE were run via the sdv-dev package or an independent reimplementation; no hyperparameter or import details given in the visible passages.

preprint-explainability-guided-augmentat.summary: A preprint proposing an explainability-guided data augmentation method to address data scarcity in cross-project defect prediction (CPDP), using semantic anchors to guide synthetic sample generation. No abstract or full text was available, so the mechanics of the augmentation pipeline and how the SDV-family tools are used cannot be confirmed. The paper cites both the CTGAN (NeurIPS 2019) and the original SDV (DSAA 2016) papers, suggesting CTGAN-style synthesis is invoked to generate augmented training data for the data-scarce defect prediction task.
preprint-explainability-guided-augmentat.needs: Full text or abstract needed to determine whether CTGAN/SDV is actually run for augmentation, used as a baseline, or merely cited; also to confirm authors' affiliations.

paper-tabbyflow-efvfm-2025.summary: Extends variational flow matching to mixed-type tables by writing the per-feature posterior as a general exponential family distribution, which turns the training objective into moment matching and so covers continuous and discrete columns in one principled form, and relates the resulting objective to generalized flow matching under Bregman divergences before evaluating the model on the standard tabular benchmark suite. CTGAN and TVAE are the GAN and VAE baselines in that suite, reported on shape and trend error rates, alpha-precision, beta-recall and machine-learning efficiency across six datasets.

preprint-lakegen-llm-tabular-corpus-2025.summary: This paper presents LAKEGEN, an LLM-based method for generating domain-specific tabular corpora with ontology-driven schemas and semantic perturbations, used to stress-test dataset discovery methods for tasks like table union search and joinability detection. The authors' prototype uses a general LLM to populate table values rather than a tabular GAN, but they note CTGAN as prior art and a possible future data-generation component. CTGAN is cited descriptively as the state-of-the-art conditional GAN approach for tabular data but is not run in the reported experiments.

preprint-not-all-features-deserve-2025.summary: This paper proposes GraDe, a method that integrates externally extracted functional-dependency graphs into an LLM's attention mechanism to better capture sparse feature interactions when generating synthetic tabular data. It reports experiments across five real-world datasets, comparing GraDe against LLM-based (GReaT) and non-LLM generators. CTGAN and TVAE, both introduced in the cited SDV-family paper, are run as baseline generators against which GraDe's synthetic data quality, machine-learning efficacy, and constraint-violation results are compared.

preprint-tabularargn-flexible-efficient-.summary: This paper from MOSTLY AI introduces TabularARGN, an auto-regressive framework for synthesizing mixed-type, multivariate and sequential tabular data that supports fairness-aware generation, imputation, and flexible conditional sampling on arbitrary column subsets. It is benchmarked against numerous state-of-the-art generators (CTGAN, STaSy, TabSyn, TabMT, ClavaDDPM, RC-TGAN, REaLTabFormer) on both flat and sequential datasets, measuring accuracy, training/generation time, and privacy. SDV's CTGAN and its relational SDV/PARSynthesizer are run as baseline generators, and SDMetrics is used to compute the paper's fidelity metrics (marginal, bivariate, and coherence accuracy).

paper-dp-llmtgen-2024.summary: Introduces a two-stage fine-tuning procedure that adapts a pretrained language model into a differentially private tabular synthesizer, first teaching the model the table's format with a non-private loss over a randomly generated table and then fitting the sensitive data under DP-SGD with a loss that masks the format tokens, and reports lower marginal error than GAN-based and marginal-based mechanisms across privacy budgets, plus a fairness-constrained generation setting reached by conditioning the prompt. CTGAN supplies two of the compared mechanisms: the authors train it under DP-SGD as DP-CTGAN and under the PATE teacher-ensemble framework as PATE-CTGAN, and both appear in every results table alongside DP-GAN, RAP, RAP++ and GSD.

paper-ecmo-virtual-patients-2024.summary: Generates virtual patients for in silico trials of medical devices used during extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, a treatment applied to too few patients for a conventional device trial. CTGAN produces the synthetic records from 767 real ECMO patients, so SDV underwrites a regulatory-adjacent use rather than a research one.

preprint-tabular-generation-models-depth.summary: This paper benchmarks five families of tabular data generation models (TVAE, CTGAN, TabDDPM, TabSyn, and SMOTE variants) across 16 diverse datasets, with extensive hyperparameter, encoding, and architecture tuning to determine how much dataset-specific optimization improves synthetic data quality and cost. It finds that diffusion-based models generally outperform others but that the advantage shrinks under a fixed GPU budget, and proposes reduced hyperparameter search spaces that retain most of the performance at far lower tuning cost. CTGAN and a customized TVAE are run as two of the five benchmarked generator families, their original cluster-based (mode-specific) normalization is examined and re-tuned, and the SDMetrics library is used to compute the paper's column-shape and pair-correlation quality metrics.
preprint-tabular-generation-models-depth.needs: TVAE was described as 'a customized version' following another paper's design, so it may be a modified reimplementation rather than the stock sdv-dev TVAESynthesizer; CTGAN appears to have been run and re-tuned more directly via its own code.

preprint-vae-gaussian-copula-vae-2023.summary: This paper proposes C2VAE, a self-supervised variational autoencoder that jointly learns disentangled representations via total-correlation-driven factorization and coupled representations via a neural Gaussian copula, using a contrastive classifier to separate the two. It targets improved disentangled representation learning across image and other datasets, addressing instability in TC-based VAE training. CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019) is cited only once in passing, in an undifferentiated list of prior VAE works applied to tabular data.

preprint-predicting-early-dropouts-activ.summary: This paper describes a machine learning approach submitted to the IFMBE Scientific Challenge 2022, predicting early dropout from an active and healthy ageing app using dynamic and static user features from the MAHA dataset. To address class imbalance, the authors compare SMOTE, ADASYN, and CTGAN as oversampling techniques for generating synthetic minority-class samples, finding CTGAN did not improve classification performance while ADASYN and SMOTE gave ~10% gains. CTGAN, run directly via the official sdv-dev/CTGAN library, is used as one of several oversampling generators evaluated against SMOTE and ADASYN.

preprint-synthetic-experience-replay-202.summary: This NeurIPS 2023 paper proposes Synthetic Experience Replay (SynthER), a diffusion-based generative model that upsamples an RL agent's collected experience to improve sample efficiency in offline and online reinforcement learning. As baselines, the authors implement and hyperparameter-tune the CTGAN and TVAE tabular synthesizers on RL replay data (D4RL halfcheetah medium-replay), using CTGAN/TVAE-specific hyperparameters (embedding dimension, discriminator steps, etc.), and adopt the marginal Kolmogorov-Smirnov and correlation-similarity evaluation statistics from the original SDV paper to assess synthetic sample fidelity. CTGAN and TVAE are run as comparison baselines against the proposed diffusion model, and SDV's evaluation methodology is cited to justify the statistics used.

paper-malicious-accounts-adversarial-blo.summary: Flags accounts behind malicious activity in permissionless blockchains from temporal and behavioural transaction features, and then asks whether the resulting detectors survive accounts that have been altered to evade them. CTGAN generates that adversarial data: it is fitted separately on each malicious activity class with default parameters and 1000 epochs, and the generated accounts are added to the test set to measure how far detector performance falls.

preprint-fast-accurate-simple-models-202.summary: The paper proposes FAST-DAD, a knowledge-distillation method that compresses complex AutoML ensemble predictors into single fast models by augmenting the training data via Gibbs sampling from a self-attention pseudolikelihood estimator. Across 30 tabular regression/classification datasets, this augmentation is compared against several alternative data-generation baselines for improving distilled student models. CTGAN, run using the original sdv-dev implementation, is one of the baseline data-augmentation methods evaluated against the authors' Gibbs-sampling approach.

thesis-money-laundering-minority-boostin.summary: Master's thesis on transaction monitoring for anti-money-laundering, where confirmed laundering is a vanishing fraction of transaction volume and every alert costs an analyst's time, so the question is whether synthesising minority-class transactions lets tree ensembles cut false positives without missing cases. Three synthesizers are employed — Gaussian Copula, CTGAN and TVAE — and the amount of generated data is varied systematically. That trio is SDV's, but the abstract names no library, so the mechanism is unconfirmed.

Because the underlying cohort cannot be published, the tutorial's working dataset is synthetic: `step1_merge_raw_sources.ipynb` builds a `SingleTableMetadata` and fits a `CTGANSynthesizer` for three hundred epochs on the merged sources.
